voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

lines.text: Ten o'clock. The academy doors open, and you've been holding this since four.
lines.say: [breathless, close, a grin in the voice] Ten o'clock. The academy doors open, and you've been holding this since four.

lines.text: What if you could see who wants you to fail?
lines.say: [quiet, level, the question laid down after the hug] What if you could see who wants you to fail?

lines.text: Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.
lines.say: [flat, hurt, each sentence its own breath] Because that's your best friend. And that's minus eighty-four.

lines.text: Since this morning, a card opens over anyone who hears your good news. You've told no one all day.
lines.say: [matter-of-fact, intimate] Since this morning, a card opens over anyone who hears your good news. You've told no one all day.

lines.text: Not because of the cards. Because he hears everything first. He always has.
lines.say: [warm, fond, a little slower on the last three words] Not because of the cards. Because he hears everything first. He always has.

lines.text: Min-jun: Knew it. Knew it.
lines.say: [delighted, breathless, boyish, half shouted into your shoulder] Knew it. Knew it.

lines.text: Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.
lines.say: [hushed, dry, the last four words slower] Sixty seconds. The card folds shut. His arm stays. So does the number.

lines.text: The rule, once. Say good news out loud, to a face, and a meter opens over whoever hears it, for sixty seconds, from plus one hundred to minus one hundred.
lines.say: [dry, exact, teacherly for one line] The rule, once. Say good news out loud, to a face, and a meter opens over whoever hears it, for sixty seconds, from plus one hundred to minus one hundred.

lines.text: Plus one hundred: pure joy for you. Minus one hundred: they want you to fail.
lines.say: [even, a beat between the two halves] Plus one hundred: pure joy for you. Minus one hundred: they want you to fail.

lines.text: It never says why. Only out loud. Only to a face. A call, a text, a post: nothing opens. Remember that.
lines.say: [measured, clipped, the last two words leaned on] It never says why. Only out loud. Only to a face. A call, a text, a post: nothing opens. Remember that.

lines.text: Every night, one chocolate bar, two halves. You take yours and watch him chew.
lines.say: [warm, amused, slow] Every night, one chocolate bar, two halves. You take yours and watch him chew.

lines.text: Your phone. Your sister. Six years of night shifts at a warehouse to pay for that classroom. You tell her.
lines.say: [softer, close, the middle sentence weighted] Your phone. Your sister. Six years of night shifts at a warehouse to pay for that classroom. You tell her.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You do. You're grinning into a phone. Nothing opens over a phone. So you still don't know her number.
lines.say: [fond, then dry on the last sentence] You do. You're grinning into a phone. Nothing opens over a phone. So you still don't know her number.

lines.text: Next morning. You've worked it out. Red is for enemies. So you test it on one.
lines.say: [brisk, amused, a plan in the voice] Next morning. You've worked it out. Red is for enemies. So you test it on one.

lines.text: The rival. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.
lines.say: [dry, half a smile] The rival. Trash-talks you every morning, two years running.

lines.text: Tae-ho: Still here?
lines.say: [bored, flat, a sneer without effort] Still here?

lines.text: You hold up the letter.
lines.say: [quick, expectant] You hold up the letter.

lines.text: Minus six. He barely looks up.
lines.say: [deflated, amused at the deflation] Minus six. He barely looks up.

lines.text: Tae-ho: Nice. Move.
lines.say: [flat, two words, already walking] Nice. Move.

lines.text: Your maths teacher.
lines.say: [quick, a new test] Your maths teacher.

lines.text: Ms. Kang: Good.
lines.say: [brief, warm underneath, clipped] Good.

lines.text: That's all you get. And it's plus forty-one.
lines.say: [surprised, a small laugh] That's all you get. And it's plus forty-one.

lines.text: So the enemy doesn't care. Why?
lines.say: [curious, leaning in] So the enemy doesn't care. Why?

lines.text: We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.
lines.say: [plain, exact, unhurried] We measure ourselves against people near our own level, not far above or below.

lines.text: And envy picks someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.
lines.say: [plain, a shade quieter] And envy picks someone who started where you did, in a thing that matters to you.

lines.text: The rival is twenty places ahead and throws that line at everyone. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.
lines.say: [dry, then quieter on the second half] The rival is twenty places ahead and throws that line at everyone. Your best friend has the next desk, the same chocolate bar, the same exam.

lines.text: But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane. The same race.
lines.say: [a turn, tighter, the hook line] But here's the problem. Problem one: the only people who can bleed at your news are the ones in your lane. The same race.

lines.text: So you ask him, on the academy steps.
lines.say: [light, a shrug] So you ask him, on the academy steps.

lines.text: He can't see it. Nobody sees the cards but you.
lines.say: [quiet, the second sentence slower] He can't see it. Nobody sees the cards but you.

lines.text: And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.
lines.say: [dry, gentle] And people don't like to admit being maliciously envious, even to themselves.

lines.text: So you have a number. And no one to ask.
lines.say: [flat, alone, the loop left open] So you have a number. And no one to ask.

lines.text: Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the jar where her paintbrushes have stood for six years.
lines.say: [hushed, tired, slowing on the brushes] Eleven. Home. The letter's already on the fridge, next to the jar where her paintbrushes have stood for six years.

lines.text: She's in the doorway, pulling on her work vest. She doesn't turn round.
lines.say: [soft, observational] She's in the doorway, pulling on her work vest. She doesn't turn round.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.
lines.say: [dry, exact, the rule remembered] You say it to her back. Nothing opens. A back is not a face.

lines.text: She laughs, and she's gone. And she still hasn't seen your face say it. Not yet.
lines.say: [warm, then a shade darker on the last two words] She laughs, and she's gone. And she still hasn't seen your face say it. Not yet.

lines.text: Minus six for the rival. So maybe the number fades the further someone is from your lane.
lines.say: [thinking aloud, curious] Minus six for the rival. So maybe the number fades the further someone is from your lane.

lines.text: This one neighbourhood in Seoul has about a thousand after-school academies.
lines.say: [dry, a little amazed] This one neighbourhood in Seoul has about a thousand after-school academies.

lines.text: And Seoul lets them teach only until ten at night. Inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.
lines.say: [dry, a smile at the inspectors] And Seoul lets them teach only until ten at night. Inspectors have patrolled the streets to make sure.

lines.text: So at ten, every door on the street opens at once.
lines.say: [building, slower, setting the picture] So at ten, every door on the street opens at once.

lines.text: So you climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd.
lines.say: [a breath held, then released on the last word] So you climb the academy steps and say it into the crowd.

lines.text: A thousand strangers. A thousand zeros. A few teal. And three red. All by the snack shop. All from your class.
lines.say: [hushed, awed, counting, the last two sentences cold] A thousand strangers. A thousand zeros. A few teal. And three red. All by the snack shop. All from your class.

lines.text: So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.
lines.say: [hard, decided, wrong] So. Minus means they want you to fail. And now you know exactly who to cut.

lines.text: The exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top 4 per cent get the top grade.
lines.say: [plain, exact] The exam grades on a curve. In most subjects, only the top four per cent get the top grade.

lines.text: So you picture your class. A hundred of you. Four places. You're fourth. He's fifth.
lines.say: [quiet, counting it out, the last two words close] So you picture your class. A hundred of you. Four places. You're fourth. He's fifth.

lines.text: So the meter becomes a weapon.
lines.say: [cold, quiet] So the meter becomes a weapon.

lines.text: Two weeks. Each mock score, you stand up, say it out loud, and read the room. Anyone who goes red, you stop helping. Stop lending notes.
lines.say: [brisk, clipped, a montage voice] Two weeks. Each mock score, you stand up, say it out loud, and read the room. Anyone who goes red, you stop helping. Stop lending notes.

lines.text: And every night at the counter:
lines.say: [a half-line, leading in] And every night at the counter:

lines.text: You climb.
lines.say: [flat, two words] You climb.

lines.text: But the higher you go, the redder the room.
lines.say: [darker, slower] But the higher you go, the redder the room.

lines.text: When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the sharper it cuts.
lines.say: [plain, exact, the last three words slower] When someone close beats you at something central to who you are, the closer they are, the sharper it cuts.

lines.text: And his number keeps going down.
lines.say: [quiet, the loop] And his number keeps going down.

lines.text: You got the place you wanted. And lost the one beside it.
lines.say: [flat, hollow, the win and the cost in one breath] You got the place you wanted. And lost the one beside it.

lines.text: The late-night study room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.
lines.say: [hushed, close, one lamp] The late-night study room. Past midnight. His seat's empty, and his notebook's open.

lines.text: You stopped helping him. He never stopped helping you.
lines.say: [quiet, the floor going out from under you] You stopped helping him. He never stopped helping you.

lines.text: He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.
lines.say: [quiet, the turn, a breath before the second sentence] He isn't sawing your chair. He's climbing.

lines.text: Envy comes in two kinds. One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down.
lines.say: [plain, exact, even] Envy comes in two kinds. One pushes you to move up. The other pushes you to pull the other person down.

lines.text: Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.
lines.say: [low, the planted line broken, slow] Minus never meant they want you to fail. It meant it hurt.

lines.text: In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.
lines.say: [plain, careful, unhurried] In one brain-scan study, envying a peer who did better at something that mattered came with activity in a region also active in pain.

lines.text: A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.
lines.say: [quiet, complete, the landing line] A card has one colour for every kind of hurt.

lines.text: But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.
lines.say: [a turn, tighter, the hook] But here's the second problem. Problem two: hurt needs a lane. Outside yours, nobody bleeds.

lines.text: And you've only ever read one lane.
lines.say: [soft, ominous, the loop] And you've only ever read one lane.

lines.text: The school confirms it. Four years, paid. If the exam holds.
lines.say: [bright, quick, a catch on the last clause] The school confirms it. Four years, paid. If the exam holds.

lines.text: For once you run home instead of to the store.
lines.say: [warm, breathless, running] For once you run home instead of to the store.

lines.text: Your sister's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.
lines.say: [tender, then a held breath on the last sentence] Your sister's at the table. A night off. You say it to her face.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.
lines.say: [stunned, flat, slow] Minus sixty-eight. Over the one person who ever asked to hear it twice.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: Ji-yoon: Say it again.

lines.text: You can't.
lines.say: [barely voiced] You can't.

lines.text: You just watched a card say what her arms didn't.
lines.say: [quiet, bitter, slow] You just watched a card say what her arms didn't.

lines.text: You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.
lines.say: [flat, each fragment colder] You take your bag. And you don't go home. Not that night. Not for a month.

lines.text: A week in the study room. You say nothing good out loud, to anyone, and the cards go quiet, because you have.
lines.say: [hushed, tired, the last clause slower] A week in the study room. You say nothing good out loud, to anyone, and the cards go quiet, because you have.

lines.text: The night before the exam. Your own notebook. Every mistake this year, and why. Leave it, or keep your place?
lines.say: [quiet, a real question, no pause after it] The night before the exam. Your own notebook. Every mistake this year, and why. Leave it, or keep your place?

lines.text: You leave it on his desk. Half a chocolate bar on top.
lines.say: [soft, decided, a small smile on the chocolate] You leave it on his desk. Half a chocolate bar on top.

lines.text: Exam day.
lines.say: [a breath, two words] Exam day.

lines.text: Last year, the country grounded its planes for 35 minutes during the English listening test. This year, you're the one listening.
lines.say: [hushed, awed, then close and personal] Last year, the country grounded its planes for thirty-five minutes during the English listening test. This year, you're the one listening.

lines.text: A country holds its breath for you.
lines.say: [quiet, complete] A country holds its breath for you.

lines.text: At your gate, in the crowd of parents: the work vest. Straight off the night shift.
lines.say: [soft, a catch on the vest] At your gate, in the crowd of parents: the work vest. Straight off the night shift.

lines.text: Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.
lines.say: [hushed, tender] Neither of you says a word. Nothing opens.

lines.text: Results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.
lines.say: [level, the loop, slower on the second sentence] Results come in a month. For a month, you say nothing to anyone.

lines.text: Results. Top grade. Top grade. Top grade. The scholarship holds.
lines.say: [tight, then released, each top grade a beat] Results. Top grade. Top grade. Top grade. The scholarship holds.

lines.text: Your best friend, beside you: top grade in maths too.
lines.say: [warm, a grin] Your best friend, beside you: top grade in maths too.

lines.text: Here's what you had backwards. You treated the four per cent like four places in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it. His grade never cost you yours.
lines.say: [slow, the penny dropping, warm on the last line] Here's what you had backwards. You treated the four per cent like four places in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top four per cent of everyone in the country who sat it. His grade never cost you yours.

lines.text: You take it.
lines.say: [soft, three words, a smile] You take it.

lines.text: In studies of regret, the most common is education: about a third of all regrets.
lines.say: [quiet, careful, looking out of the window] In studies of regret, the most common is education: about a third of all regrets.

lines.text: Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.
lines.say: [quiet, landing on her] Her brushes have stood in a jar for six years.

lines.text: Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the warehouse and say it to her face.
lines.say: [level, the dilemma, both halves given equal weight] Text her, and never see her colour again. Or take the bus to the warehouse and say it to her face.

lines.text: A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.
lines.say: [low, tempting, slow] A text would open nothing. You could keep her forever on a screen.

lines.text: You're on the bus.
lines.say: [decided, quick, no pause before it] You're on the bus.

lines.text: Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the loading dock. And you say it.
lines.say: [hushed, steady, a breath before the last sentence] Six o'clock. Her shift ends. You stand on the loading dock. And you say it.

lines.text: The same.
lines.say: [flat, two words, no surprise] The same.

lines.text: She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.
lines.say: [warm, slow, the turn in your body] She holds on. And this time you don't go stiff.

lines.text: Ji-yoon: Say it again.
lines.say: [bright, laughing, hungry for it] Say it again.

lines.text: You do.
lines.say: [barely there, close] You do.

lines.text: You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.
lines.say: [low, after the silence, the planted line brought back] You said nobody outside your lane bleeds.

lines.text: She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.
lines.say: [quiet, complete, the landing line, slow] She was never outside your lane. She was in it first.

lines.text: Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.
lines.say: [soft, a picture] Six years ago it was her letter on the fridge.

lines.text: At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.
lines.say: [plain, exact, gentle, slower through the last two sentences] At the nineteen ninety-two Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver. Silver thinks of the gold it nearly won. Bronze thinks of nearly winning nothing.

lines.text: She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.
lines.say: [tender, slow, the last sentence almost whispered] She's not watching you fail. She's watching the life she handed you walk up the dock with the news. And she wants it in.

lines.text: The same number. The same arms. You hold on through the second sixty.
lines.say: [quiet, steady, complete] The same number. The same arms. You hold on through the second sixty.

lines.text: Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.
lines.say: [hushed, morning-light, slow on the last three words] Morning. The fridge. She unpins the calendar, and behind it is a letter. Hers. Six years old.

lines.text: For once, silence leaves both of you in the room.
lines.say: [soft, close, warm] For once, silence leaves both of you in the room.

lines.text: Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.
lines.say: [quiet, to the viewer, slow] Tomorrow someone you love will pause half a second before they say congratulations.

lines.text: That half-second is the other life, going past.
lines.say: [hushed, complete, the residue] That half-second is the other life, going past.

lines.text: Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it. For the first time, the good news isn't yours.
lines.say: [light, quick, a smile that is about to stop] Then the door. Your best friend. A letter of his own. He says it. For the first time, the good news isn't yours.

lines.text: So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
lines.say: [warm, direct, unhurried, no hype] So, would you still say it to her face? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have done the same, hit like and subscribe.
